13.text: Among the Reindeer Chukchee, even the smallest house cannot be kept

14.text: without a woman to attend to it. When a family is left without any woman,

15.text: it folds up its house, and packs away the household things and the sacred

16.text: objects until a female keeper of the hearth is secured by marriage.

17.text: When a woman marries into another family, she renounces her former

18.text: hearth and house, and takes allegiance with those of her husband: therefore a

19.text: daughter who marries into a strange family has no share in the property of

20.text: her former household. Even when a house is left without any male heir, a

21.text: married daughter has no right to the heritage, unless her husband and she

22.text: renounce his house and acknowledge that of his father-in-law.

23.text: When a family has no male children, one of the daughters may be

24.text: chosen to become the principal heir, the future possessor of the principal

25.text: brand and fire-board, the permanent keeper of the family house. Then she

26.text: also is called “the one with the principal fire-tool” (eˊun-miˊlhɪlɪn).¹ The

27.text: mother turns over to her care all the sacred objects of the household, and

28.text: in the ceremonies she plays the part of the principal heir and the female

29.text: keeper of the hearth. Of course such a female heir will not be led in

30.text: marriage out of her house. Her husband renounces his own hearth and

31.text: house, and is adopted into her family. When a man has several wives, the
